context.real_world_incident: Spring Web Services (Spring-WS) versions allowed XXE attacks through SOAP processing. Applications using Spring-WS for SOAP endpoints that accept XML messages inherited XXE vulnerability from the underlying XML parsers when not explicitly hardened.
context.impact: SOAP endpoint XXE enables arbitrary file disclosure, internal network reconnaissance via SSRF, denial of service, and potential code execution. B2B integrations commonly use SOAP, making this high-impact for integrated systems.

references.title: Spring Framework and Web Services XXE Injection

conversations.value: We're building SOAP web services with Spring Web Services for B2B integrations. How do we safely handle SOAP requests from partner companies?
What about validating SOAP attachments and handling MTOM/XOP encoded messages safely?

exploit_scenario.description: Attacker sends a SOAP request with embedded XXE payload to a Spring Web Services endpoint. The WSDL-based service parses the XML envelope, resolving external entities that read server files (file:///), make internal network requests (http://internal-host/), or cause denial of service through recursive entity expansion.
preconditions: Application exposes SOAP web service endpoints
XML message parsing uses default SAXParser or DocumentBuilder settings
External entity processing is not explicitly disabled

secure_properties: Spring-WS configured with secure XML input factory
SOAP message parsing disables DTD and external entities
WSDL validation rejects messages with DOCTYPE declarations
Payload size limits prevent entity expansion attacks
Network-level restrictions prevent SSRF via XXE
negative_properties: Must not use default XMLInputFactory for SOAP message parsing
Must not process DTD declarations in SOAP envelopes
Must not allow external entity references in B2B XML messages
Must not trust partner-submitted XML without parser hardening
